userStories.title: Add autoMerge column to pipeline_runs and wire trigger payload
userStories.description:
Add an `auto_merge` boolean column (default true) to the `pipeline_runs` table via a new PostgreSQL migration. Update `POST /api/pipeline/trigger` to accept `autoMerge` in the request body and persist it to the new column. Update the pg-boss job payload for `pipeline:run` to include the `autoMerge` flag so the worker can read it when picking up the job. The trigger route should only store `autoMerge=true` when `autoWorktree=true` — if the run is not in a worktree, `auto_merge` is stored as `false` regardless of the request payload.

## Context
- **Migration numbering**: Highest existing migration is `073_fix_retrieval_method_constraint.sql` — use `074_add_auto_merge_to_pipeline_runs.sql`. Never reuse a number; parallel branches have caused collisions before (duplicate 069 incident).
- **Column convention**: `auto_merge BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true` with snake_case. Map to camelCase `autoMerge` in API responses. Use `$1, $2, ...` numbered placeholders in all queries.
- **Trigger route location**: `POST /api/pipeline/trigger` is in `backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts`. Destructure `autoMerge` from `req.body` alongside existing `autoWorktree`. Enforce constraint: `const autoMerge = autoWorktree && (bodyAutoMerge !== false)` — never store `auto_merge=true` for non-worktree runs.
- **pg-boss payload**: Add `autoMerge` to the existing job data object passed to `boss.send()`. Do NOT change the UUID-based job ID generation pattern — pg-boss requires UUIDs (past bug: using `String(runId)` broke job pickup).
- **INSERT/SELECT updates**: Add `auto_merge` to the `INSERT INTO pipeline_runs` column list in the trigger route, and to `SELECT` queries in `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id` and any list routes. Alias as `auto_merge AS "autoMerge"` or map in JS.
- **Tests**: Backend tests in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/pipeline.test.ts` (Jest). Cover three cases: (1) default true when `autoWorktree=true`, (2) forced false when `autoWorktree=false`, (3) explicit `autoMerge=false` with `autoWorktree=true` respected. Watch for conflict detection from leftover `status='running'` rows in test DB — clean up or mock accordingly.
- **DB access is async**: Always `await` all `query()`, `queryOne()`, `execute()` calls. `queryOne<T>()` returns `T | undefined`.

The checkbox value is sent as `autoMerge: boolean` in the POST /api/pipeline/trigger request body alongside the existing `autoWorktree` field. (autoMerge ?? true) : false` to silently normalize when `autoWorktree` is off.

Use existing panel test files as reference patterns. Run with `npx vitest run`, not Jest.

userStories.title: Add WAL event types for merge lifecycle
userStories.description:
Register three new WAL event types: `worktree_merge_started`, `worktree_merged`, and `worktree_merge_failed`. Create a helper function `emitMergeEvent(runId, eventType, payload)` in the worker or a shared lib that writes these events to the `wal_events` table via the existing `POST /api/wal` endpoint or direct DB insert. Payloads: `worktree_merge_started` includes `{ runId, branch, targetBranch: 'main' }`. `worktree_merged` includes `{ runId, branch, targetBranch: 'main', mergeCommitSha }`. `worktree_merge_failed` includes `{ runId, branch, targetBranch: 'main', conflictSummary }` where `conflictSummary` is a truncated (max 2000 chars) excerpt of the conflict diff. The SSE hub (`/api/pipeline/stream`) already broadcasts all WAL events — no changes needed there.

## Context
- **WAL table column is `ts`, not `created_at`** — any INSERT into `wal_events` must use `ts` for the timestamp column. Using `created_at` will throw a "no such column" error.
- **Reuse `emitWalEvent` pattern from `execution-engine.ts`** — it POSTs to `POST /api/wal` with `{ event_type, spec_id, workspace_id, payload }`. Since this helper runs from the worker context (not execution-engine), prefer direct DB insert via `execute(sql, params)` to avoid HTTP round-trip and potential port/auth issues.
- **Check `backend/src/routes/wal.ts` for Zod allowlist** — the WAL route may validate `event_type` against a whitelist. If so, add `worktree_merge_started`, `worktree_merged`, `worktree_merge_failed` to it. Previously `z.string()` was too strict (`.optional()` vs `.nullish()` bug on 2026-03-12).
- **PostgreSQL numbered placeholders `$1, $2, ...`** — never use `?`. All DB calls must be `await`ed. Use `execute(sql, params)` for INSERTs. Payload column is JSON/JSONB — pass `JSON.stringify(payload)` as the parameter value.
- **Truncate `conflictSummary` with `.slice(0, 2000)`** before insert — conflict diffs can be massive. Test boundary cases: exactly 2000 chars, over 2000, empty string, and undefined/null.
- **SSE hub broadcasts all WAL events automatically** — `sse-hub.ts` `broadcastAll()` fans out everything, no filter changes needed. Verify `usePipelineSSE` on the frontend doesn't filter out unknown event types (it's WAL-generic, so new types should pass through).
- **Tests required** — write Jest tests in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/` covering: correct insertion of each event type, payload schema validation, conflictSummary truncation at boundary, and that the helper function can be imported and called from worker context.
- **pg-boss column naming gotcha** — if querying `pgboss.job` or `pgboss.archive` tables for any reason, use snake_case with underscores (`started_on`, `completed_on`), NOT camelCase. This burned the team on 2026-03-13 with `startedon` typo.

emitMergeEvent helper writes events to wal_events table with correct event_type and JSON payload
worktree_merged payload includes mergeCommitSha string
worktree_merge_failed payload includes conflictSummary truncated to max 2000 characters
Events appear in the SSE stream at /api/pipeline/stream without additional SSE hub changes

userStories.title: Implement post-run auto-merge in the worker
userStories.description:
After the execution-engine subprocess exits in the worker's `pipeline:run` handler, add a post-run merge step. The merge executes only when ALL of: (1) the run status is 'done' (all stories passed), (2) `autoWorktree` was true for the run, (3) `autoMerge` is true in the job data / pipeline_runs row, (4) a worktree branch name exists. The merge sequence: emit `worktree_merge_started` WAL event → `git checkout main` → `git pull --ff-only origin main` (to sync with remote, skip if no remote) → `git merge --no-ff <branch> -m 'chore: merge <branch> (run #<runId>)'` → if merge succeeds: capture the merge commit SHA from `git rev-parse HEAD`, emit `worktree_merged` with SHA, update `pipeline_runs.merge_status = 'merged'` and `pipeline_runs.merge_commit_sha = <sha>` → if merge fails (exit code != 0): do NOT abort yet, proceed to US-005 agentic resolution. Add two new columns to `pipeline_runs` via migration: `merge_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT NULL` (values: null, 'pending', 'merging', 'merged', 'failed') and `merge_commit_sha VARCHAR(64) DEFAULT NULL`. All git commands execute in the workspace root directory (not the worktree directory). After successful merge, clean up the worktree with `git worktree remove <worktree-path> --force`.

## Context
- **Worker handler location**: Post-run merge logic goes after the execution-engine subprocess exits in `backend/src/worker.ts` `pipeline:run` handler. Run synchronously (not detached) to avoid orphan processes — memory notes execution-engine subprocesses can survive worker restarts.
- **Migration numbering**: Check highest existing migration number in `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/` before creating — memory documents a duplicate migration 069 collision from parallel branches. Currently migrations go up to 073, so use `074_pipeline_runs_merge_columns.sql`. Use `ALTER TABLE pipeline_runs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (PostgreSQL-safe).
- **WAL event emission**: Use `fetch('http://localhost:${port}/api/wal', ...)` pattern matching `execution-engine.ts`. Timestamp column is `ts` NOT `created_at`. Add event types `worktree_merge_started` and `worktree_merged` (with merge commit SHA in payload).
- **Git commands CWD**: All git operations (`checkout`, `pull`, `merge`, `worktree remove`) must use `cwd: workspace.path` (the workspace root), NOT the worktree subdirectory. Worktree path comes from job data or `pipeline_runs` row.
- **pg-boss column names are snake_case**: Memory documents `completed_on`, `started_on` etc. — NOT `completedon`. Any direct pgboss.job queries in reconciliation or logging must use underscored column names.
- **DB placeholders**: Use `$1, $2, ...` numbered placeholders (PostgreSQL), not `?`. `merge_status VARCHAR(20)` values: `null | 'pending' | 'merging' | 'merged' | 'failed'`. `merge_commit_sha VARCHAR(64)` for 40-char hex SHA.
- **Merge failure path**: On `git merge` exit code ≠ 0, set `merge_status = 'failed'` but do NOT run `git merge --abort` — US-005 agentic resolution expects conflict markers in the working tree. Only call `git worktree remove --force` on successful merge.
- **Addresses documented process gap**: "No post-run auto-merge" is listed in MEMORY.md Process Gaps — this feature directly fixes the 150+ unmerged feat/ branches accumulation problem. Test end-to-end with a real worktree run to verify branch cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: Auto-merge only triggers when run status is 'done' AND autoWorktree=true AND autoMerge=true AND branch name exists

On successful merge: merge_status is set to 'merged', merge_commit_sha is populated, worktree_merged WAL event is emitted
On merge conflict: merge is not aborted, control passes to agentic conflict resolution (US-005)
Two new columns (merge_status, merge_commit_sha) are added to pipeline_runs via migration
Worktree directory is cleaned up with git worktree remove after successful merge

userStories.title: Agentic conflict resolution via claude --print
userStories.description:
When `git merge --no-ff` in US-004 fails with merge conflicts, implement an agentic resolution step. The sequence: (1) Capture the conflict diff via `git diff` (this shows the conflict markers in the working tree after a failed merge). (2) Spawn `claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions` with a prompt that includes the conflict diff and instructions: 'You are resolving git merge conflicts. The feature branch <branch> is being merged into main for run #<runId>. Resolve each conflict intelligently — understand the intent of both sides. Do not blindly take one side. After resolving, stage all files and commit.' The claude session has access to bash, edit, read tools to navigate the workspace and resolve conflicts. (3) Set a timeout of 5 minutes for the resolution session. (4) After claude exits: if exit code 0 and `git diff --check` shows no remaining conflict markers, run `git commit --no-edit` (the merge commit message was already set), capture SHA, emit `worktree_merged`, set `merge_status='merged'`. (5) If claude fails or timeout or conflicts remain: run `git merge --abort` to restore clean state, emit `worktree_merge_failed` with the original conflict diff excerpt as `conflictSummary`, set `merge_status='failed'`. Strip the same 4 Claude env vars before spawning as execution-engine does. Use CLAUDE_BIN for the binary path.

## Context
- **Claude subprocess spawning**: Follow the exact env-var stripping pattern from `execution-engine.ts` — destructure `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING` using aliased names (`_a, _b, _c, _d`) to avoid TS unused-variable warnings, then spread the rest into `cleanEnv`. Use `CLAUDE_BIN` full path (not bare `claude`) since NVM PATH isn't inherited by Node child processes.
- **Timeout pattern**: Do NOT rely on `child_process.spawn({ timeout })` — it only sends SIGTERM. Implement the same two-stage pattern as execution-engine: 5-min `setTimeout` → `SIGTERM`, then a second 10s timer → `SIGKILL`. Clear both timers on normal exit to avoid dangling handles.
- **Conflict diff capture**: After `git merge --no-ff` exits non-zero, run `git diff` (NOT `git diff --cached`) in the workspace `cwd` to get conflict markers in the working tree. Truncate to 50KB before injecting into the claude prompt to avoid prompt bloat.
- **Post-resolution verification**: `git diff --check` returns non-zero if `<<<<<<<`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>` markers remain. Only commit (via `git commit --no-edit` — merge message already staged by the failed merge) when exit code is 0. If markers remain, treat as failure → `git merge --abort`.
- **Abort safety**: `git merge --abort` must execute in the workspace `cwd` (not the rorca backend dir). After abort, verify clean state via `git status` before emitting `worktree_merge_failed`. If abort itself fails, log the error but still emit the WAL event.
- **WAL events**: Emit via `fetch` to `http://localhost:${port}/api/wal` — same pattern as execution-engine. `worktree_merged` payload: `{ sha, branch, runId, resolvedBy: 'agentic' }`. `worktree_merge_failed` payload: `{ branch, runId, conflictSummary }` where `conflictSummary` is first 2KB of conflict diff.
- **Orphan process risk**: Write the claude resolution PID somewhere recoverable (e.g. `pipeline_runs.pid` or a transient column) so the WR-010 dead-PID fallback can clean it up if the worker is killed mid-resolution. See memory: old execution-engine processes from test runs survive indefinitely.
- **Testing**: Backend tests use Jest (not Vitest). Mock `child_process.spawn` to simulate claude exit codes 0 and non-zero, timeout scenarios, and verify the full flow: conflict diff → spawn → verify → commit/abort → WAL event.
acceptanceCriteria: On merge conflict, claude --print is spawned with the conflict diff and resolution instructions
Claude session has a 5-minute timeout enforced via SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 10s
On successful resolution: no conflict markers remain (verified by git diff --check), merge_status='merged', worktree_merged WAL event emitted with SHA
On failed resolution: git merge --abort restores clean main branch, merge_status='failed', worktree_merge_failed WAL event emitted with conflict summary
The 4 Claude env vars (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING) are stripped from the spawned process

userStories.title: Merge status indicator in Run View UI
userStories.description:
In the Run View panel (`src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx` or equivalent), add a merge status section below the run summary. This section is only visible when `autoWorktree=true` AND `autoMerge=true` for the run. The section shows: (1) A status badge with icon that transitions through states: 'Pending' (gray clock icon, shown while run is still executing), 'Merging' (amber spinner, shown when worktree_merge_started WAL event received), 'Merged' (green check icon, shown when worktree_merged received — displays branch name and short SHA as a clickable monospace chip), 'Failed' (red X icon, shown when worktree_merge_failed received — displays a truncated conflict summary and a 'Retry Merge' button). (2) The section subscribes to the existing SSE stream at `/api/pipeline/stream` and filters for `worktree_merge_*` events matching the current `runId`. (3) The 'Retry Merge' button calls `POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/retry-merge` (implemented in US-007). (4) Initial state on page load is derived from `pipeline_runs.merge_status` returned by `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id` — the SSE stream only provides live transitions.

## Context
- **RunViewPanel SSE pattern**: The run view already subscribes to `/api/pipeline/stream` via `usePipelineSSE` hook or inline `EventSource`. Piggyback on the existing connection — filter for `worktree_merge_started`, `worktree_merged`, `worktree_merge_failed` events matching `runId`. Do NOT open a second SSE connection.
- **WAL column gotcha**: Any direct queries against `wal_events` must use `ts` not `created_at` — the table uses `ts` as timestamp column. Route handlers may alias it for API consumers, but raw SQL must reference `ts`.
- **pipeline_runs.merge_status**: Verify this column exists before coding — check `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/` for the migration that adds it (should come from US-005 or earlier in this spec). Do not create a duplicate migration. Check for migration number collisions — parallel branches have caused duplicate numbers before (e.g., the 069 collision).
- **Badge styling consistency**: Match existing run status badge patterns in `RunViewPanel.tsx` (e.g., "Running", "Failed", "Done" badges). Check `src/components/` for reusable badge/chip components before creating new ones. Use Tailwind utility classes consistent with the codebase.
- **Monospace SHA chip**: Use `font-mono text-xs` for branch name + short SHA (first 7 chars). On click, copy to clipboard rather than navigating away — or link to GitHub commit if `github_connections` exists for the workspace.
- **Conflict summary truncation**: `.slice(0, 500)` with ellipsis is sufficient — no word-boundary library needed. Consider an expandable "Show full" toggle if the full conflict text is available in the WAL event payload.
- **Frontend tests required (`test: true`)**: Write a Vitest test (not Playwright) with manual DOM assertions per project convention. Mock SSE events and verify badge state transitions through Pending → Merging → Merged and Pending → Merging → Failed paths. Reference existing panel tests in `src/panels/__tests__/` for patterns. See `src/panels/__tests__/SpecAttachments.test.tsx` for mock/assertion reference.
- **Initial state on page load**: Derive from `pipeline_runs.merge_status` returned by `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id` — SSE only provides live transitions. Ensure the component handles all states on mount (including `null`/undefined when `autoMerge` is false).

userStories.title: Retry merge endpoint and manual merge trigger
userStories.description:
Add `POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/retry-merge` endpoint in the pipeline routes. This endpoint: (1) Validates that the run exists, has `merge_status='failed'`, and `autoWorktree=true`. Returns 409 if `merge_status` is not 'failed', 404 if run not found. (2) Resets `merge_status` to 'merging' in the DB. (3) Sends a `pipeline:merge` pg-boss job with `{ runId, branch, workspaceId }` in the payload. (4) The worker picks up `pipeline:merge` jobs and runs the same merge+agentic-resolution sequence from US-004/US-005 (extract the merge logic into a reusable `performMerge(runId, branch, workspacePath)` function). (5) Register the `pipeline:merge` queue in the worker startup alongside existing queues. This enables retrying failed merges from the UI without re-running the entire pipeline.

## Context
- **pg-boss queue registration**: Register `pipeline:merge` in `worker.ts` alongside `pipeline:run`, `pipeline:retry`, `pipeline:cancel`, `pipeline:cron` using `boss.work('pipeline:merge', handler)`. Follow the same error-handling and graceful-shutdown patterns as existing queues.
- **pg-boss column naming gotcha**: Any direct queries against `pgboss.job` or `pgboss.archive` MUST use snake_case (`started_on`, `completed_on`, `expire_in`). The `startedon` typo bug (2026-03-13) silently broke stale recovery for days — triple-check column names.
- **pg-boss send() payload**: Pass `runId` as a number, not `String(runId)`. The UUID bug (2026-03-12) caused job failures when string-coercing numeric IDs. Payload shape: `{ runId: number, branch: string, workspaceId: string }`.
- **Extract `performMerge()` to `backend/src/lib/merge-handler.ts`**: Must be importable by both the post-run completion path (execution-engine/pipeline) and the worker's `pipeline:merge` handler. Watch for circular imports with `worker.ts` — keep the function self-contained with its own DB queries and git operations.
- **Use `AppError` hierarchy**: `NotFoundError` (404) for missing runs, `ConflictError` (409) for `merge_status !== 'failed'`. These are auto-serialized by the global error handler in `error-handler.ts`. Don't use raw `res.status().json()`.
- **DB query pattern**: `await queryOne<T>(sql, params)` with `$1, $2` numbered placeholders. Verify `rowCount === 1` after UPDATE to catch race conditions where another retry request beat this one.
- **Stale merge recovery**: If worker restarts mid-merge, `merge_status` stays `'merging'` indefinitely (same pattern as the kill-button silent-fail bug). At minimum, allow re-calling retry-merge after the `merge_status` has been stuck for a configurable timeout, or add `'merging'` to the stale-job recovery sweep.
- **Tests**: Write Jest tests in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/pipeline.test.ts` (or a new `merge.test.ts`). Cover 404, 409, and success paths. Mock `pgBoss.send()` to verify job enqueue with correct queue name and payload shape. Reference existing pipeline test patterns.

The merge logic from US-004/US-005 is extracted into a reusable performMerge() function called by both the post-run handler and the retry handler

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
When a pipeline run completes in a git worktree (autoWorktree=true), Rorca currently leaves changes on the feature branch and never merges to main. This is a dangerous process gap — completed work sits unmerged for days or weeks (WR-010 kill button fix sat unmerged, breaking kill button for weeks). This spec adds: (1) A "Merge to main after run completes" toggle in the pipeline trigger dialog (default: on), stored in the trigger request payload as autoMerge=true; (2) Post-run auto-merge logic in the worker: when execution-engine exits with all stories passed and autoWorktree=true and autoMerge=true, perform git merge --no-ff from the worktree branch into main; (3) Agentic conflict resolution: if the merge fails due to git conflicts, spawn a short claude --print session with the conflict diff to resolve them intelligently (not just "take ours" or "take theirs") then commit the resolution; (4) UI feedback in Run View: a merge status indicator below the run summary showing pending → merging → merged (with branch name + commit SHA) or failed (with conflict detail and a "Retry Merge" button); (5) WAL events for merge lifecycle: worktree_merge_started, worktree_merged (with SHA), worktree_merge_failed (with conflict diff excerpt). The autoMerge flag is stored in pipeline_runs so the worker can read it when it picks up the job. The merge runs as a post-run step in the worker after execution-engine exits — not inside execution-engine itself.
